items.title: Inquest into death of Jamal Francique hears from Peel region constable
items.summary: , nearly seven years ago is hearing from a constable who arrived at the scene after the shooting. , on Aug. 23, 2020. , nearly seven years ago is hearing from a constable who arrived at the scene after the shooting. Const. Marc Charlebois was one of the members of the Peel regional police tactical unit dispatched to a townhouse complex after 28-year-old Jamal Francique was shot during an attempted arrest the evening of Jan. 7, 2020. Charlebois says he heard when he arrived that there had been an officer-involved shooting and a collision, and that police couldn’t see inside the vehicle that crashed because it was nighttime and the car’s windows were tinted. The inquest heard last week that police had planned an operation to arrest Francique for allegedly violating one of the conditions of his bail, but the officer who was meant to block in his car was late. According to an agreed narrative read on Friday, several plainclothes officers on foot and in unmarked cars moved in to contain Francique’s car as he tried to drive away, and one of the officers on foot fired his gun four times. One of the bullets hit Francique in the head. The inquest heard Francique’s car veered sharply and crashed into the pillar of a nearby garage, and a tactical unit and ambulance were then called in.

items.title: Mississauga’s data centre moratorium facing challenge from American company
items.summary: An American-based logistics company is taking the city of Mississauga to the Ontario Land Tribunal, looking to overturn the municipality’s one-year moratorium on artificial intelligence data centres. Prologis, a San Francisco-based supply chain warehouse developer, filed an application in 2025 to build a two-storey, 220,000 sq. ft. data centre on what used to be farmland in the Tenth Line and Argentia Road area. The proposal was met with pushback from the local city councillor, who claimed the facility would have 14 generators and possibly contain lithium-ion batteries, raising noise and environmental concerns. “Is it a power plant or a data centre? What’s the noise going to be like? ” Ward 9 councillor Martin Reid previously told Global News. Mississauga, subsequently, became one of the first municipalities in Canada to adopt a data centre moratorium when city council voted unanimously to impose a one-year ban, which came into effect in September. ” When council enacted the pause, it instructed staff to come back with a study on the impacts of hosting data centres in the city. Prologis seems to be frustrated with the pace at which the city is moving to finish that study and address its concerns with data centres. The company says the instructions given to staffers were too broad, and that the city has not provided updates on its status.

items.title: Violent home invasion in Ontario town leads to arrest of 2 Mississauga men
items.summary: Two Mississauga men face a rash of charges in connection with a police investigation into an armed home invasion east of Oshawa last Thursday afternoon. m. on Nov. 12. ” The home is located in the area of Meadowview Boulevard and Scugog Street. Three suspects were spotted fleeing the area as police officers arrived on the scene. “Following a brief pursuit, one suspect was taken into custody,” police said in a news release, adding the suspect was found in possession of a firearm with a prohibited over-capacity magazine. A second suspect was located later and taken into custody without incident, police added. Several schools in the area were put into hold-and-secure mode as a precaution as officers searched for a third suspect. Police conducted an “extensive search of the area” with the assistance of tactical, canine and drone officers, but were not able to locate the suspect.

items.title: Sunny skies and double-digit highs ahead for Toronto, Mississauga and GTA this week
items.summary: Residents across the GTA and Hamilton can look forward to a mostly sunny week, with daytime highs climbing into the double digits, according to Environment Canada. After a cool start, with lows around 1 C across most of the region tonight (Sunday, Nov. 15) and near zero in Hamilton, the week begins with plenty of sunshine on Monday (Nov. 16). Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington will see a high of 11 C on Monday, with winds becoming west at 20 km/h in the afternoon. Hamilton and Durham Region will be a little cooler, with highs of 9 C under a mix of sun and cloud in Hamilton and mainly sunny skies in Durham. The sunshine continues on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with highs between 10 C and 12 C across the region and clear skies overnight. Wednesday (Nov. 18) is expected to be one of the warmest days of the week, with sunny skies and a high of 13 C in Toronto and 12 C in Mississauga, Brampton, Burlington, Hamilton and Durham. Overnight lows will stay above freezing, around 3 C to 4 C. Thursday (Nov. 19) will bring more sun, with highs of 12 C in most areas and 13 C in Hamilton. Clouds will roll in Thursday night, with lows of 5 C to 6 C.

items.title: Peel's Child Care Fees Have Already Dropped 53 Percent, But $10-a-Day Target Slips to 2027
items.summary: According to Peel Region's 2026-2029 Early Years and Child Care business plan, daily fees across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon have already fallen about 53 per cent since 2024 and are capped at 22 dollars a day since January 2025. The region says that saves a family with a toddler and a preschooler roughly 19,372 dollars a year, though the province's goal of 10 dollars a day won't arrive until 2027. Peel runs 53,276 licensed child care spaces across 556 centres and 387 home-based sites, and children make up 42 per cent of its population, the highest share in the GTA, the plan says. The region must add 10,768 new spaces for children under six between 2024 and 2026, and about 60 per cent of those are approved, leaving just over 4,000 to go. Peel also says it needs roughly 1,245 more early years staff, and that hiring remains difficult because wages lag behind school boards.

items.title: Peel Police Respond to Person in Crisis at Mississauga Hotel Near Pearson Airport
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel Regional Police were called to a hotel near Toronto Pearson International Airport's Terminal 3 in Mississauga on Sunday for what officers describe as an incident involving a person in crisis. The outlet reported a large police presence remains in the area as the situation unfolds. Police said there is no threat to public safety and asked anyone nearby to follow directions from officers at the scene, according to insauga.com. Officers have not released which hotel is involved or identified the person, the outlet said. Police said more updates would be shared as they become available, insauga.com reported. The outlet listed the occurrence number as PR260387337 and noted that anyone in distress can reach Canada's 988 suicide crisis helpline, or EveryMind's 24/7 crisis line in Peel at 905-278-9036.

items.title: Mayor-Elect Tedjo Joins Ford to Open Ontario's Largest Grocery Store in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Now Toronto, Food World Plus opened to shoppers on Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East, becoming Ontario's largest grocery store at 176,000 square feet. The outlet reported the store centers its selling point on global food, stocking products from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Now Toronto said the store aims to save Mississauga's diverse population from visiting multiple specialty grocers for hard to find ingredients. Beyond groceries, the store includes a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and an in house butcher, according to the outlet. Mayor elect Alvin Tedjo attended the grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford, Now Toronto reported. The outlet noted the meat department includes a dedicated halal section, with meat sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards.

items.title: Extra Daily Math and Literacy Time Lifts EQAO Scores at Toronto and Peel Schools
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a Toronto elementary school and a Mississauga school in the Peel District School Board dramatically improved their EQAO test scores, and the newspaper drew lessons from both. The outlet detailed Corvette Junior Public School in Scarborough, where a balanced day schedule gives students 100 minutes of uninterrupted math daily, 40 more than the province requires, plus 100 minutes for literacy. The Star reported the extra math time allows for longer lessons and group work that help teachers identify struggling students. In one example, Grade 5 and 6 students worked in small groups on a word problem, writing equations and checking answers with addition. A student identified as Shaun told the Star that math is fun even when it is challenging. The newspaper said similar lessons were drawn from Mississauga's Brian W. Fleming school within the Peel board.
